Messages.Author: Oaflord
Messages.Body:
Hey fellow Meths,

After a long and hard battle, the table is down to two meths, one pool each,
and the player whose turn it is currently, knows they will lose next turn.
The Meth decides to call Conservative Agitation (1 pool for each) and get a
draw. Is that 1 victory point each (9.1 VTES Rules) or is it 1/2 victory
point each (similar to an Intentional Draw 3.7 VEKN Rules)?

Just curious...

oAFLORD
aka
Thomas Kuster
V:EKN Prince of Caledon

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"Oaflord" <oaf...@sprint.ca> wrote:
> Hey fellow Meths,
>
> [...]the table is down to two meths, one pool each,
> and the player whose turn it is [thinks she] will lose next turn.

> The Meth decides to call Conservative Agitation (1 pool for each)
> and get a draw. Is that 1 victory point each (9.1 VTES Rules) or
> is it 1/2 victory point each (similar to an Intentional Draw 3.7
> VEKN Rules)?

1 VP each (for ousting their respective preys).

The case is only a "draw" inasfar as the term means "tie for 1st".
It is not an "Intentional Draw", which is a term used only for the
conditions specified in the V:EKN rules (as far as this game is
concerned, anyway).

Messages.Author: Sorrow
Messages.Body:
> After a long and hard battle, the table is down to two meths, one pool
each,
> and the player whose turn it is currently, knows they will lose next turn.

> The Meth decides to call Conservative Agitation (1 pool for each) and get
a
> draw. Is that 1 victory point each (9.1 VTES Rules) or is it 1/2 victory
> point each (similar to an Intentional Draw 3.7 VEKN Rules)?

It's not a draw. The game is over when all meths are ousted and the
winner is the meth with the most VPs. If 2 or more meths have the
same number of VPs, it is a tie and not a draw. From the section you
quote above (9.1):

"Exception: If a player is ousted at the same time that her prey is ousted,
the player gets the ante and victory point but does not gain six pool."

So the game is over and each gets 1 VP.

Sorrow
